correctness.rationale: In the stated invariant cube let s=X−Z, p=X, q=−Z. The opinion equations force s=u(a+q)=v(a+p)≥0. At s=0 the distinct anchors exclude common nonzero opinion; the only solution is the origin. At s>0 leadership values are interior, and elimination gives (a−p)p²=(a−q)q²=s³/ρ. Equality factors into p=q or pq=s(s−a), so the unequal case requires ρ=s²/(a−s)² and discriminant s(4a−3s). The root s− lies below a for every ρ>0; s+ is admissible and distinct only for √ρ>4, and the coalesced root at equality is already counted. The symmetric and antisymmetric sectors of the full Jacobian give two negative eigenvalues in the polarized sector and a negative transverse trace with determinant of sign ρ−16. At the exact witness, principal-minor computations reproduce the three characteristic polynomials; the symmetric and same-sign branches are strictly Hurwitz, while the cross-sign asymmetric quartic has negative constant term, hence a positive real root. Exchange-negation supplies the twin spectra. The origin is not attracting even relative to the cube: in X=−Z=r,u=v=y, y′=r²[α−(α+4β)y], so arbitrarily close initial points with 0<y<α/(α+4β) cannot converge to y=0. The result is local for fixed anchors; neither nonlinear behavior at equality nor accessibility from the physical initial-opinion plane follows.
